title: Measuring the Marginal Detection Benefit of Sandboxed Emulation for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to measure the marginal detection benefit of adding automated sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for intent→configuration artifacts generated by an LLM. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and using the declared model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses) we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded outcomes lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, an explicit clarification of provider-call auditing fields, an artifact-grounded attribution for the single discordant pair, and bounded operational implications and limitations.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Practical deployments must ensure that generated artifacts satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and higher‑order safety or policy invariants. A common operational mitigation is a generate→validate→(repair)→execute workflow, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports document this pattern but provide limited preregistered, paired measurements of the marginal value added by emulation when the same generated candidate is examined by both conditions [1]–[3].

Research question and contributions. Our preregistered question was: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired-binary confirmatory design and faithful autonomous execution; (2) artifact-grounded quantitative results on Npairs = 720; (3) a concise clarification of provider-call audit fields and exact run accounting; (4) an artifact-grounded attribution of the single discordant episode and conservative operational recommendations and limitations.
sections.related_work: Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools. Surveys and architectural reports emphasize that LLM-generated NetOps artifacts require layered V&V: syntactic parsing, sequence/workflow constraints, invariants (e.g., keep‑one‑uplink‑up), and dynamic runtime properties may need different primitives [1]. Prototype tool reports show that generate→validate→repair patterns and emulator-assisted checking are common mitigations; gains are heterogeneous and depend on task regimes, validator coverage, and emulator fidelity [2]. Empirical evidence from adjacent domains (program verification, configuration analysis) indicates that pairing generation with deterministic verifiers or execution harnesses can improve correctness but leaves open how much incremental coverage sandboxed execution provides when a strong validator already exists [3]. Our paired shared_initial_candidate design isolates only downstream guarded-stage contributions, complementing these prior findings.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. We preregistered a paired-binary design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory items. The plan targeted Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440) and a minimum effect-of-interest of 0.20 for power planning; handling of parser failures, deterministic reseeding, exclusions, multiplicity control for exploratory tests, and contamination checks were fixed in the preregistration.

Task bank, vendors, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. Confirmatory tasks were deterministically generated from the intent_configuration_repair_v1 family and spanned three abstracted vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates. Inclusion required vendor parser acceptance after deterministic reseeding (up to two attempts). Shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: for each pair a single sampled initial candidate (one model call) was produced and reused by both downstream conditions; this isolates only downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation or permitted repair) as sources of between-condition discordance.

Model and validator. The declared/requested model was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider: openai_responses); model_configuration archived requested max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature recorded as null (no explicit client-supplied temperature). The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) is a deterministic rule engine that performs vendor-CLI parsing, command canonicalization, sequence-order checks, workflow‑policy checks (make-before-break, all_down_before_any_field_change, minimum_active_in_groups), protected-interface invariants, and final-state conformance. The validator outputs a binary detection flag under the preregistered scoring rule full_intent_constraint_validation and emits a per-episode validator_trace.

Guarded pipeline and sandboxed emulation. The guarded pipeline ran the baseline validator and then executed the same candidate in a sandboxed emulation harness instantiated with the declared topology template. The emulator records runtime observations (admin transitions, transient concurrent states, MTU/VLAN application effects, simple reachability indicators) and maps them to runtime-observation rules that can trigger guarded detections when they reveal violations not codified in the static validator. The emulation mapping is intentionally conservative: it aims to surface runtime-only policy violations rather than to generate speculative alarms.

Provider-call auditing and explicit clarification. The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation include a provider_call_audit object. To avoid ambiguity: stage_counts enumerates calls by orchestration stage (e.g., "shared_initial_generation": 720, "repair": 1). Condition_counts reported in that audit are stage‑attribution counters from the orchestration viewpoint (for this run they appear as "shared": 720 and "guarded": 1) and should be read as counts of model calls attributable to the shared-initial stage and to guarded-stage (repair) calls respectively, not as episode counts for the guarded experimental arm. Episode accounting is reported separately: completed_episode_count = 1440 and complete_pair_count = 720. The canonical reconciliation artifact confirms: model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial calls plus 1 repair-stage call), cache_miss_count = 721, and zero failed hosted model calls. This explanation reconciles apparent audit asymmetries and directly ties stage_counts to the single repair invocation observed in the confirmatory run.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact-grounded). Analysis artifacts report contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values are taken verbatim from analysis/results.json and the archived analysis artifacts.

Run accounting and discordant-pair attribution. Provider-call audit and deterministic_reconciliation identify a single repair-stage invocation (stage_counts: repair = 1) corresponding to the unique n10 discordant count. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the permissible causes for that single guarded-only detection are: (i) a guarded-stage emulation observation not encoded as a validator rule, or (ii) the single documented repair-stage invocation that modified or augmented the candidate before guarded scoring. The raw per-episode artifacts (execution/raw_results.jsonl) contain the validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields for that pair_id; deterministic_reconciliation links that pair_id to the single repair-stage call. The archived execution bundle is the authoritative source for the detailed per-episode trace.

Representative diagnostics. Representative scoring traces (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) show normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_count fields. For the majority of confirmatory pairs the validator_trace shows violation_count = 0 and final-state conformance; these traces explain the baseline ceiling effect (719/720). The single discordant trace can be inspected in the archived raw_results file to determine whether the guarded detection was emulation-driven or repair-driven; the preregistered artifacts provide that mapping without the need for additional experiments.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The artifact-grounded evidence supports three proximate explanations:

1) Validator ceiling effect. The deterministic validator encoded the workflow-level checks exercised by this curated task bank (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore and make_before_break_uplink_switchover). The baseline success rate of 719/720 (0.9986111111111111) left effectively no headroom for the guarded emulation to flag additional failures in this constrained regime.

2) Curated inclusion policy. Confirmatory items required parser acceptance before inclusion; deterministic_reconciliation reports zero irrecoverable parser exclusions. This produced a tight, parser-validated sample where many runtime-only faults typical of adversarial or noisy inputs are underrepresented.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair. The design reused identical initial candidates across both conditions; provider_call_audit confirms model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair). The unique n10 discordance therefore localizes to a single downstream event (emulation observation or the one repair call) rather than to generation variability.

Operational implications. For operator regimes that maintain a strong, workflow-aware static validator and that enforce parser-level inclusion policies, the incremental detection yield of adding automated sandboxed emulation can be vanishingly small. This does not negate the value of sandboxing: selective guarded emulation remains valuable for high-risk changes, adversarial stress testing, or when inputs are noisy or uncurated. Practically, operators should (a) invest in validator coverage for common workflow constraints when low-latency generation is required, (b) employ guarded emulation selectively for high-impact operations, and (c) use adversarial/fuzzing task banks to expose validator gaps. The archived representative traces supply concrete seeds for such follow-up efforts.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) to the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call) and the single discordant episode is traceable in the archived raw_results artifact. We interpret this near-zero marginal effect as arising from validator ceiling effects and the curated, parser-validated task design. Whether guarded stages add substantive operational value in noisier, adversarial, or multi‑vendor production-like regimes remains an open empirical question; the archived execution bundle provides reproducible starting points for targeted follow-up studies.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across model or validator families.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream guarded-stage contributions but intentionally remove between-condition generation variability; this design constrains the sources of discordance to emulation observations or repair-stage calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulation could alter outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for the preregistered regime.
